correctness.rationale: Every selected set is partitioned into four disjoint cases by presence of the distinguished B vertex and the number (zero/one/at least two) of selected A vertices. Degree computation n-1 versus n-2 makes those cases necessary and sufficient, without omissions. Contributions add to the stated polynomial. Lowest exponents give the exact minimum and multiplicities, including \(n=3\) and \(n=4\) boundary cases. A standalone graph-based test enumerated all 174752 vertex subsets for \(3\le n\le9\) with coefficient-by-coefficient agreement; the finite test corroborates rather than proves the general formula.

originality.rationale: The studied family is matching-deleted complete bipartite crowns after one vertex deletion. Originality is limited to the complete residual strong-domination set classification, its cardinality polynomial and minimizer counts. The motivating stability paper explicitly treats ordinary K_(m,n) and the non-bipartite cocktail-party graph K_(2n)-M, not the crown K_(n,n)-M. The 2022 vertex-modification paper proves bounds on minimum numbers, not this cardinality distribution. The 2020 queen-crown paper studies K_(m,2), a different graph despite a similar term. Accessible indexed mathematical records concerned different domination predicates on crowns or a different graph family. Unavailable pertinent 2023 full text is a genuine unresolved priority risk, not represented as cleared.

value.rationale: The natural new invariant is the complete degree-sensitive strong-domination distribution after a vertex is removed from a highly symmetric standard matching-deleted bipartite graph, directly motivated by recent vertex-deletion stability research. It determines all set counts and all minimum-set types for every order, not only the stable/unstable scalar property. The result exhibits a nontrivial degree-class obstruction, the small-order \(n=3\)/\(n=4\) transitions, and a closed general polynomial; it is not a parameter renaming, one numeric table entry, or a trivial corollary of the known stability bounds.
